title: Experiential Bhutan | Free Gangtey Gompa Monastery Excursion
highlights: Discover the natural beauty of the Land of the Thunder Dragon, from Thimphu's vibrant streets to Punakha Dzong's beauty and the iconic Tiger’s Nest in Paro.
Marvel at the majestic 177-ft Buddha Dordenma Statue in Thimphu, one of the world's tallest Buddha statues and offering stunning views of the Thimphu Valley.
Visit Punakha Dzong, nestled at the confluence of the Mo Chhu and Pho Chhu rivers, where intricate carvings and vibrant murals tell the rich history of the kingdom.
Get a chance to witness the black-necked cranes as you explore Gangatey’s Phobjikha Valley, a vast wetland, rich in biodiversity with amazing landscapes.
Enjoy a thrilling hike to Taktsang Monastery, also known as Tiger’s Nest, an iconic pilgrimage site that offers amazing views of the Paro Valley.
overview:
About the tour:
Bhutan's immaculate landscapes form a masterpiece of marvels, spanning from lush forests to crystalline rivers. Immerse in the tapestry of cultural festivities, relish in the flavours of spicy cuisine, and soak in the genuine warmth of smiles exchanged. Allow Bhutan's enchanting allure to enfold you, presenting an array of experiences that will eternally grace your dreams of exploration.

Kindly carry a valid photo ID proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.
Images are for representation purpose only.
Kindly do not litter and help keep the destinations clean.
It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.

If in case any traveller wants to or decides to leave the trip in the middle, all the expenses from the point onwards will be borne by the traveller. Neither the operator nor Thrillophilia will be held responsible for such decisions or for any refund.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Day at Leisure
days.desc: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon arrival at the Bagdogra Airport/New Jalpaiguri Railway Station, board your transfer to the beautiful Phuntsholing Border Town. After checking in to your hotel, spend the rest of the day at leisure, where you can visit the Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre and witness the rare and endangered crocodiles up close. Also, you can stroll along the serene Torsa Riverside and soak-in its amazing atmosphere. Later, return to your hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Day at Leisure
days.desc: After check-out, get driven to the immigration office and obtain your Bhutan travel permit. Then, enjoy a scenic journey to Thimphu, the capital city of Bhutan. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and spend the rest of your day at leisure. You can head out and explore the Dechen Phodrang Monastery or admire traditional arts at the National Institute for Zorig Chusum. Also, you can wander through the lush Royal Botanical Garden, or soak in the cozy vibe of the Ambient Café, savoring local food.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, delve into Thimphu’s cultural charm on a sightseeing tour, beginning with the National Memorial Chorten—a revered monument. Next, encounter the unique takin, Bhutan’s national animal, at the Motithang Takin Preserve, nestled amid pine forests. Also, discover intricate local artistry at the Handicrafts Emporium, where every piece reflects Bhutan’s deep-rooted heritage. After the sightseeing tour, you can visit the Bhutan Postal Museum and marvel at the stunning talking stamps.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass | Punakha Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Check out & get driven to Punakha. En route, pause at the iconic Dochula Pass—known for its 108 memorial chortens. Upon arrival in Punakha, visit Chimi Lhakhang, known as the "Fertility Temple," & continue to the Punakha Dzong, one of Bhutan’s most beautiful fortresses & stroll across the iconic Punakha Suspension Bridge, known for its scenic river views. Also, you can opt for a thrilling river rafting experience on the Pho Chhu Mo Chhu river before getting driven to your hotel for check-in.

days.title: Day Trip to Gangtey
days.desc: Today, enjoy a scenic drive to Gangtey, known for its natural beauty. Start with a visit to the Phobjikha Valley, a stunning glacial valley, home to the rare Tibetan black-necked cranes. Next, visit the iconic Gangtey Gompa Monastery and soak-in the views of the Phobjikha Valley. Continue to Wangdiphodrang Dzong, a fortress that stands at the confluence of the Mo Chhu and Tang Chhu rivers. Also, admire its stunning Bhutanese architecture before getting transferred to your hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get transferred to Paro, passing through charming Bhutanese villages. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and later, enjoy a sightseeing tour. Start with a visit to the Drukgyel Dzong, an iconic fortress offering a glimpse into Bhutan's military past. Next, pay your respects at the Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples, dating back to the 7th century. After an amazing day, get transferred to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Set off on a scenic drive to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang, the starting point of the legendary Tiger’s Nest hike. Once there, trek through pine-scented forests and fluttering prayer flags, with dramatic glimpses of the cliff-perched monastery guiding your way. On arrival, explore its sacred chambers and meditation caves honoring Guru Rinpoche. After descending, return to your hotel, where you can unwind with a traditional hot stone bath or savor Bhutanese cuisine at Park 76 Café & Pub.
